identity.title: Circumstellar Disks around Binary Stars in Taurus

paper_type_evidence.quote: We have conducted a survey of 17 wide ($>$ 100 AU) young binary systems in Taurus with the Atacama Large Millimeter Array (ALMA) at two wavelengths.

targets.name: 17 wide Taurus binaries (e.g. FV Tau, UY Aur, HK Tau, DK Tau, IRAS 04113+2758)

coordinates.value: per-source positions in Table 3 (e.g. FV Tau A 4:26:53.550 +26:06:53.903 J2000)

evidence.quote: We selected targets from a single star formation region, Taurus (distance $\sim$ 140 pc)
We selected targets from a single star formation region, Taurus (distance $\sim$ 140 pc)

distance_source.value: adopted Taurus distance; d = 140 pc used to compare with Andrews et al. 2013

evidence.quote: We selected targets from a single star formation region, Taurus (distance $\sim$ 140 pc)

question.value: What are the circumstellar disk masses of wide young binary components in Taurus, and how do primary and secondary disks compare with each other and with single stars?

evidence.quote: The observations were designed to measure the masses of circumstellar disks in these systems as an aid to understanding the role of multiplicity in star and planet formation.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00150.S.

bands.value: Band 6 (1.3 mm) and Band 7 (850 um), ALMA Cycle 0

evidence.quote: we have obtained ALMA Cycle 0 observations of 17 young binary systems in Taurus for which the components can be resolved.
At 1.3 mm (Band 6), one of the correlator basebands was set to cover the CO(2-1) transition at 230.5 GHz

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: 4 basebands, each 1.875 GHz total bandwidth, 488 kHz channels; one baseband on CO(2-1) in Band 6 and CO(3-2) in Band 7

evidence.quote: The correlator was configured with each of the four basebands covering a total bandwidth of 1.875 GHz with a channel spacing of 488 kHz.
one of the correlator basebands was set to cover the CO(2-1) transition at 230.5 GHz
one baseband covered CO(3-2) at 345.8 GHz

angular_resolution.value: Beams ~1.1x0.74 arcsec at 1.3 mm; ~0.7-0.9x0.5 arcsec at 850 um

max_recoverable_scale.value: 3.0 arcsec at 850 um and 4.4 arcsec at 1.3 mm

evidence.quote: the maximum scale for extended emission to be detected was 3.0$''$ at 850 $\mu$m and 4.4$''$ at 1.3 mm.

sensitivity.value: rms 0.15-0.20 mJy/beam at 1.3 mm; 0.35-0.40 mJy/beam at 850 um

evidence.quote: The typical rms values achieved are 0.15-0.20 mJy/beam at 1.3 mm and 0.35-0.40 mJy/beam at 850 $\mu$m

time_on_source.value: 60 s at 1.3 mm and 90 s at 850 um per source

evidence.quote: Given the short time on source (60 sec at 1.3 mm and 90 sec at 850 $\mu$m)

observing_dates.value: Table 1 lists data sets 2012-12-05 to 2013-01-26 (Dec 2012 - Jan 2013; April 2012 for one set)

what.value: Stellar luminosities and masses (Siess et al. 2000 grid) for sources

evidence.quote: We adopt the stellar luminosities and masses from (cite: and13) for our sources
Millimeter fluxes are single-dish fluxes at 850 $\mu$m taken from (cite: and05)

what.value: Comparison sample of single Taurus stars, with known multiples removed

evidence.quote: we used the sample in (cite: and13), and removed all known multiple sources using the list in (cite: kra11)

pipeline_or_manual.value: CASA with scripts provided by the NRAO ALMA center, standard scripts

evidence.quote: Data for each band were calibrated separately using the CASA package and scripts provided by the NRAO ALMA center.

flux_calibrator.value: Callisto, Butler-JPL-Horizons 2012 models; zero-spacing flux 8.54 Jy (1.3 mm), 19.45 Jy (850 um)

evidence.quote: The absolute flux calibration used Callisto and the Butler-JPL-Horizons 2012 flux models
a 5% absolute flux calibration uncertainty (ALMA memo 594)

self_calibration.value: Phase-only self-calibration using bright reference sources per data set; continuum time-averaged to a single point

evidence.quote: Each data set had at least one target with sufficient continuum flux to allow phase-only self-calibration, which was applied after the other calibrations.
Continuum and CO images at each band were generated using the *clean* task within CASA
with a robust beam weighting of 0.5

masking.value: Interactive clean, 50 iterations per cycle, boxes only on emission in dirty map; stop when residuals in boxes at or below image rms

evidence.quote: images were generated interactively with 50 iterations per cycle and clean boxes placed only around emission visible in the dirty map.
The primary beam correction was applied and the entire primary beam was mapped for each source

array_combination.value: FV Tau and HBC 387 pointings combined in a mosaic

evidence.quote: we combined the two observations in a mosaic, increasing the sensitivity.

final_beam.value: Default restoring beam (Gaussian fit to dirty beam), listed in Table 2

evidence.quote: The images use the default restoring beam, which is a Gaussian fit to the dirty beam.

evidence.quote: we also adopt the (cite: and13) scaling of $T_d = 25 (L_{\ast}/L_{\odot})^{-1/4}$ K.

method.value: Interactive clean with robust 0.5, primary-beam corrected

method.value: 2D Gaussian fits in the image plane; point source if major-axis uncertainty exceeds fit size; upper limits 3 sigma

fitting.value: Gaussian least squares in image plane

evidence.quote: we fit these data in the image plane to determine the total flux and size. The clean continuum maps at each band were fit with two-dimensional Gaussians for each source using the CASA routine *imfit*.

findings_qualitative.value: No substantial circumbinary emission detected in any system

evidence.quote: there is no evidence for substantial circumbinary emission in any of these systems.

claims.hypothesis: Do binary disks follow the stellar-mass to mm-flux scaling of single Taurus stars?
claims.experiment: Compare ALMA fluxes and masses with Andrews et al. 2013 singles using survival analysis
claims.result: Primaries consistent with singles (20-60%); secondaries lower (8-17%)
claims.finding: Binary sample matches the scaling within the scatter

evidence.quote: the disks from this binary sample match the scaling between stellar mass and millimeter flux of F$_{mm} \propto$ M$_{\ast}^{1.5-2.0}$ to within the scatter found in previous studies.

claims.hypothesis: Is the primary disk always more massive than the secondary disk?
claims.experiment: Compare secondary/primary flux and mass ratios in 15 bona fide binaries
claims.result: Secondary flux higher in two systems; three by disk mass
claims.finding: Not always; counter to some theory

evidence.quote: in three systems, the circumsecondary disk is more massive than the circumprimary disk, counter to some theoretical predictions.

claims.hypothesis: Are secondary/primary disk mass ratios correlated with stellar mass ratios?

evidence.quote: the secondary/primary stellar and disk mass *ratios* are not correlated

why_this_method.value: Image-plane fitting used since CASA does not allow multi-component uv fitting and goal was overall flux and mass

evidence.quote: because CASA does not currently allow multiple component fitting in the uv-plane, we fit these data in the image plane to determine the total flux and size.

limitations_admitted.value: Primary/secondary comparison may be biased by lower stellar mass of secondaries; observations not designed to characterize disk physical parameters or extended emission

evidence.quote: the comparison of the primaries and secondaries may be significantly biased by the lower stellar mass for the secondaries.

referee_caveats_inferred: Single-temperature optically thin masses with fixed opacity are uncertain, especially for bright, possibly optically thick disks
Stellar masses inherited from model grids with large uncertainties
